title: संखुवासभा जिल्ला आँखिभुई गा.वि.स. का याख्खा जातिका बालबालिकाहरुको शैक्षिक अवस्था {Sankhuwasabha Jilla Ankhibhui Ga.Bi.Sa. Ka Yakhkha Balbalikaharuko Shaikshyik Awastha}
authors: पोखरेल  Pokhrel, दीपक कुमार Deepak Kumar
nepali: नेपाल चार जात छत्तिस वर्णको साझा फूलबारी हो । यहाँ विभिन्न जातजाति, भाषाभाषि, धर्म, संस्कृति बोकेका मानिसहरु बस्दछन् । यिनीहरु मध्येको एउटा याख्खा जाति आफ्नै छुट्टै मौलिकता र संस्कृति भएको जाति हो । अध्ययनकर्ताको याख्खा जातिको बारेमा यो अध्ययनमा केन्द्रित गरिएको थियो । यो अध्ययनको शीर्षक ‘संखुवासभा जिल्ला आँखिभुई गा.वि.स. का याख्खा जातिका बालबालिकाहरुको शैक्षिक अवस्था’ छनौट गरिएको थियो । यस अध्ययनमा याख्खा बालबालिकाहरुको शैक्षिक सहभागिताको स्थिति (भर्नादर, कक्षा छाड्ने र कक्षा दोहो¥याउने दर, विद्यालय उपस्थिति), शैक्षिक उपलब्धि स्तर तथा प्राथमिक विद्यालय सहभागितामा देखिएका पहिचान गर्ने उद्देश्यहरु समावेश गरिएका थिए । अध्ययनका उद्देश्यहरुसंग सम्बन्धित सूचनाहरु संकलन गर्न अन्तर्वार्ता निर्देशिका, विद्यार्थी विवरण फारम तथा घरधुरी सर्वेक्षण फारम जस्ता सूचना संकलनका साधनहरुको निर्माण गरि प्रयोग गरिएको थियो । सूचनादाताहरुको रुपमा अध्ययन क्षेत्रमा २० जना शिक्षक, ४० जना अभिभावकहरु र ४० जना विद्यार्थीहरुलाई छनौट गरिएको थियो । अध्ययन क्षेत्रको रुपमा संखुवासभा जिल्लाको आँखिभुई गा.वि.स. का ४ वटा विद्यालयहरुलाई छनौट गरिएको थियो । अध्ययन क्षेत्रका याख्खा बालबालिकाहरुको औसत भर्नादर ५७ प्रतिशत देखियो । त्यसैगरी याख्खा बालबालिकाहरुको कक्षा छाड्नेदर ४.५३ प्रतिशत र कक्षा दोहो¥याउने दर १५.७३ प्रतिशत देखियो । याख्खा बालबालिकाहरुले कक्षा छाड्ने र दोहो¥याउने कारणहरु बालबालिकाहरु विद्यालयमा बारम्बार अनुत्तिर्ण हुनु, घरको पढ्ने वातावरण उपयुक्त नहुनु, घरको काममा बढी समय दिनु पर्ने, विद्यालयमा नियमित रुपमा पढाइ नहुनु, घरको आर्थिक अवस्था कमजोर हुनु आदि पाइयो । याख्खा बालबालिकाहरुको वार्षिक उपस्थिति दर केटाहरुको ६५.०३ देखि ६९.१४ सम्म देखियो भने केटीहरुको ६४.१३ देखि ६९.०९ प्रतिशत सम्म देखियो । याख्खा छात्र वा छात्राहरुको वार्षिक उपस्थिति दरमा धेरै अन्तर देखिएन । याख्खा बालबालिकाहरु नियमित रुपमा उपस्थित नहुने कारणहरु सानो उमेर, विद्यालय टाढा, घरको कामको व्यस्तता, आर्थिक अभाव, विद्यालयमा पढ्ने वातावरण राम्रो नहुनु आदि देखियो । अध्ययन क्षेत्रका याख्खा बालबालिकाहरुको शैक्षिक उपलब्धि अध्ययन गर्दा ६६.६० प्रतिशत उत्तिर्णदर र ३२.८७ प्रतिशत अनुत्तिर्णदर देखियो भने गैर याख्खाहरुको उत्तिर्णदर ७०.३६ र अनुत्तिर्णदर २६.६९ प्रतिशत देखियो । प्राथमिक विद्यालयमा याख्खा बालबालिकाहरुको शैक्षिक निरन्तरता न्यून रहेको पाइयो । याख्खा बालबालिकाहरुको शैक्षिक सहभागितामा देखिएका समस्याहरु भित्र भाषिक कठिनाइ, पढाइ कमजोर, बालबालिकाहरुको पढाइप्रति अभिभावकहरुले चासो नदिनु, गृहकार्य नियमित नगर्नु, घर परिवारमा निर्देशन गर्ने अभिभावकहरुको अभाव, घर परिवारमा पढ्ने वातावरण नहुनु जस्ता पक्षहरु देखियो । विद्यालयमा याख्खा बालबालिकाहरुको भर्नादर बढाउन, कक्षा छाड्ने र दोहो¥याउने दर घटाउन, शैक्षिक उपलब्धिस्तर राम्रो बनाउन तथा शैक्षिक सहभागितामा देखिएका समस्याहरु कम गर्न बालबालिकाहरुका लागि विशेष शिक्षाको व्यवस्था गर्ने, मातृभाषामा प्राथमिक शिक्षा दिने व्यवस्था कार्यान्वयन गर्नुपर्ने, विद्यालयमा छात्रवृत्ति, पोशाक, प्रशंसा र हौसला बढाउने कार्यक्रम संचालन गरिनु पर्ने आवश्यकता देखियो ।
american_english:
Nepal is a shared garden of four castes and thirty-six varnas.
People carrying various castes, languages, religions and cultures live here.
One of them, the Yakhkha caste, is a caste with its own distinct originality and culture.
The researcher's [interest in] the Yakhkha caste was made the focus of this study.
The title of this study was chosen as "The Educational Status of Yakhkha Caste Children of Ankhibhui VDC, Sankhuwasabha District."
This study included objectives to identify the status of educational participation of Yakhkha children (enrollment rate, dropout and repetition rates, school attendance), the level of educational achievement, and what was seen in primary school participation.
To collect information related to the objectives of the study, information collection tools such as an interview guide, student details form and household survey form were developed and used.
As informants, 20 teachers, 40 parents and 40 students were selected in the study area.
As the study area, four schools of Ankhibhui VDC in Sankhuwasabha district were selected.
The average enrollment rate of Yakhkha children in the study area was seen to be 57 percent.
Likewise, the dropout rate of Yakhkha children was seen to be 4.53 percent and the repetition rate 15.73 percent.
The reasons for Yakhkha children dropping out and repeating were found to be children failing repeatedly at school, an unsuitable study environment at home, having to spend more time on household work, teaching not taking place regularly at school, weak economic condition of the home, and so on.
The annual attendance rate of Yakhkha children was seen to range from 65.03 to 69.14 for boys, while for girls it was seen to range from 64.13 to 69.09 percent.
No great difference was seen in the annual attendance rate of Yakhkha boys or girls.
The reasons for Yakhkha children not attending regularly were seen to be young age, the school being far away, busyness with household work, economic hardship, a poor study environment at school, and so on.
When studying the educational achievement of Yakhkha children in the study area, a pass rate of 66.60 percent and a fail rate of 32.87 percent were seen, while the pass rate of non-Yakhkhas was 70.36 and the fail rate 26.69 percent.
The educational continuity of Yakhkha children in primary school was found to be low.
Among the problems seen in the educational participation of Yakhkha children were language difficulty, weak studies, parents not taking interest in their children's studies, not doing homework regularly, a lack of parents to give guidance in the family, and no study environment in the family.
To increase the enrollment rate of Yakhkha children in school, reduce the dropout and repetition rates, improve the level of educational achievement and reduce the problems seen in educational participation, the need was seen to arrange special education for the children, implement provision of primary education in the mother tongue, and run programs in schools for scholarships, uniforms, praise and encouragement.
british_english:
Nepal is a common garden of four castes and thirty-six varnas.
Here live people who carry different castes, tongues, faiths and cultures.
One among them, the Yakhkha caste, is a caste possessing its own separate originality and culture.
The researcher's concern with the Yakhkha caste was made the focus of this study.
The title of this study was chosen as 'The Educational Condition of Yakhkha Caste Children of Ankhibhui VDC, Sankhuwasabha District'.
The study set itself the objectives of identifying the state of educational participation of Yakhkha children (enrolment rate, rates of leaving and repeating a class, school attendance), the level of educational attainment, and what has been observed in primary school participation.
In order to gather information relating to the objectives of the study, instruments of information collection such as an interview schedule, a pupil particulars form and a household survey form were devised and employed.
As informants in the study area, twenty teachers, forty parents and forty pupils were selected.
As the area of study, four schools of Ankhibhui VDC in Sankhuwasabha district were selected.
The average enrolment rate of Yakhkha children in the study area was found to be 57 per cent.
Similarly, the rate of leaving class among Yakhkha children was found to be 4.53 per cent and the rate of repeating a class 15.73 per cent.
The causes of Yakhkha children leaving and repeating classes were found to be repeated failure of the children at school, an unsuitable environment for study at home, having to devote more time to household chores, teaching not being carried on regularly at school, the weak financial position of the household, and the like.
The annual attendance rate of Yakhkha children was found to range from 65.03 to 69.14 in the case of boys, whereas in the case of girls it was found to range from 64.13 to 69.09 per cent.
No great difference was observed in the annual attendance rate of Yakhkha boys or girls.
The causes of Yakhkha children not being present regularly were found to be tender age, the distance of the school, pressure of household work, financial deprivation, a poor environment for study at school, and the like.
On examining the educational attainment of Yakhkha children in the study area, a pass rate of 66.60 per cent and a failure rate of 32.87 per cent were observed, whilst the pass rate of non-Yakhkhas was 70.36 and the failure rate 26.69 per cent.
Educational continuity among Yakhkha children at primary school was found to be low.
Among the problems observed in the educational participation of Yakhkha children were language difficulty, weak attainment, parents taking no interest in their children's studies, homework not done regularly, an absence of parents to give direction within the family, and no environment for study in the home.
In order to raise the enrolment rate of Yakhkha children at school, lower the rates of leaving and repeating class, improve the level of educational attainment and lessen the problems observed in educational participation, the need was seen to make special educational provision for the children, to implement provision for primary education in the mother tongue, and to run programmes of scholarships, uniform, praise and encouragement in the schools.
australian_english:
Nepal is one big shared garden of four castes and thirty-six varnas.
People from all sorts of castes, languages, religions and cultures live here.
One of those groups, the Yakhkha caste, has its own separate identity and culture.
This study put the researcher's focus on the Yakhkha caste.
The study was titled "The Educational Situation of Yakhkha Caste Children in Ankhibhui VDC, Sankhuwasabha District."
The study aimed to identify where Yakhkha children stand with educational participation (enrolment rate, class dropout and repetition rates, school attendance), their level of educational achievement, and what shows up in primary school participation.
To collect information tied to the study's aims, data collection tools were built and used: an interview guide, a student details form and a household survey form.
In the study area, 20 teachers, 40 parents and 40 students were picked as informants.
Four schools in Ankhibhui VDC of Sankhuwasabha district were picked as the study area.
The average enrolment rate for Yakhkha children in the study area came out at 57 per cent.
In the same way, the Yakhkha children's class dropout rate came out at 4.53 per cent and the repetition rate at 15.73 per cent.
The reasons Yakhkha children drop out and repeat came out as: kids failing at school over and over, a home study setup that doesn't work, having to put in more time on housework, teaching not happening regularly at school, a weak household financial situation, and so on.
The annual attendance rate for Yakhkha children came out at 65.03 to 69.14 for boys, while for girls it came out at 64.13 to 69.09 per cent.
There wasn't much difference in the annual attendance rate between Yakhkha boys and girls.
The reasons Yakhkha children don't turn up regularly came out as: being young, the school being a long way off, being flat out with housework, money problems, a poor study setup at school, and so on.
Looking at the educational achievement of Yakhkha children in the study area, the pass rate came out at 66.60 per cent and the fail rate at 32.87 per cent, while non-Yakhkha students had a pass rate of 70.36 and a fail rate of 26.69 per cent.
Yakhkha children's educational continuity at primary school came out low.
The problems showing up in Yakhkha children's educational participation included language difficulty, weak study skills, parents not taking an interest in their kids' schooling, homework not done regularly, no parents at home to give direction, and no study setup in the home.
To lift the enrolment rate of Yakhkha children at school, cut the dropout and repetition rates, improve educational achievement and reduce the problems showing up in educational participation, the study saw a need to set up special education for the children, bring in primary education in the mother tongue, and run scholarship, uniform, praise and encouragement programs in schools.
informal_english: Right, so Nepal's a big shared garden of four castes and thirty-six varnas, and there's people of all sorts of castes, languages, religions and cultures living there. One of those groups is the Yakhkha caste, and they've their own distinctive identity and culture. That's what this study is about. It's called "The Educational Situation of Yakhkha Caste Children in Ankhibhui VDC, Sankhuwasabha District." The study wanted to find out how Yakhkha children are doing with school — enrolment, dropping out, repeating classes, attendance — along with their achievement levels and whatever shows up in primary school. To get the information, they put together an interview guide, a student details form and a household survey form, and used those. They picked 20 teachers, 40 parents and 40 students as informants, and four schools in Ankhibhui VDC in Sankhuwasabha district as the study area. The average enrolment rate for Yakhkha children came out at 57 per cent. The dropout rate was 4.53 per cent and the repetition rate 15.73 per cent. The reasons behind the dropping out and repeating were things like the kids failing again and again, no decent place to study at home, too much housework, teaching not happening regularly at school, and the family being hard up. Attendance ran from 65.03 to 69.14 per cent for boys and 64.13 to 69.09 per cent for girls, so there wasn't much difference between them. The reasons they weren't turning up regularly were being young, the school being far away, being busy with housework, money troubles, and a poor study setup at school. On achievement, Yakhkha children had a 66.60 per cent pass rate and a 32.87 per cent fail rate, while non-Yakhkha children had 70.36 per cent passing and 26.69 per cent failing. Educational continuity at primary level was low for Yakhkha children. The problems they face include language difficulties, weak study skills, parents not taking an interest, homework not getting done, no one at home to guide them, and no study setup at home. To fix all that, the study says there's a need for special education for the children, primary education in the mother tongue, and school programmes for scholarships, uniforms, praise and encouragement.
translator_notes: Source spells the caste 'याख्खा' (Yakhkha); kept consistently. One clause in the source ('प्राथमिक विद्यालय सहभागितामा देखिएका पहिचान गर्ने') is elliptical and rendered as identifying what is seen in primary participation.
